text: Plumb must be installable via both pip and uv with the package name plumb-dev on PyPI and the CLI command plumb.
Plumb must support loading environment variables from .env files to manage configuration settings including ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
The plumb init command must create a .env file in the project directory to facilitate environment-based configuration management.
Tests must be linked to requirements through requirement ID comments in the format plumb:req-XXXXXXXX to establish traceability between test functions and specific requirements.
All tests must be organized in the tests/ directory with specific test files for each component.
Tests without requirement links must be treated as sync violations that indicate either missing requirements or unnecessary tests.
The system must support file ignore patterns through a .plumbignore file.
The plumb approve command must provide a --all option to approve all changes at once.
Generated cache and coverage files must be excluded from commits.
The system must include a check command as an alias for manual decision scanning.
Plumb must read transcripts from several coding agents through per-agent TraceSource adapters.
The system must handle conversations that span multiple session files including exit-and-relaunch scenarios.
The sync command must provide progress indicators with status updates to give users feedback during operation.
The workflow must require an explicit sync step after approving decisions with staging of sync output before re-committing changes.
The system must use a branch-sharded structure for decision logs.
The plumb merge-decisions branch command must allow users to merge decisions from feature branches back to main.
A find_decision_branch function must help locate which branch file contains a specific decision ID.
The core LLM integration must use a WholeFileSpecUpdater that takes full spec content and decisions as input and outputs section_updates for existing sections and new_sections for brand new sections.
The system must include an OutlineMerger component to handle structural changes when new sections need to be added or content needs reordering.
The system must include helper functions _clean_duckdb_row() and _to_python_native() to convert DuckDB result types to Python native types for Pydantic compatibility.
Comprehensive test coverage must be implemented for migration and merge functionality including edge cases and error conditions.
The conversation log parser must preserve full tool call information from every supported agent's transcripts.
Tool calls must be normalized to a ToolCall record with name, category, file_path, file_paths, input_summary, and result_summary using a nine-category tool taxonomy.
Tool results must be preserved in truncated form when the agent records them to enable deterministic file_refs population and improve decision extraction quality.
Plumb must be simple over clever and solve a bounded problem holdable in a single programmer's head.
All LLM-powered functions must be implemented as DSPy programs not open-ended agents to ensure they are controllable auditable and reliable.
Plumb must address models with litellm strings so any provider litellm supports can serve inference.
Anthropic's Claude Haiku 4.5 (anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5) must be the default model for all programs.
The model config field must set the model and per-program overrides must be configured in program_models.
Plumb must operate as a git hook and CLI tool and must not change how the user writes code.
The commit must be canonical: in review mode the pre-commit hook ensures that every committed state has been reviewed and approved.
A commit must represent a fully reconciled snapshot of spec tests and code.
Conversation analysis must be opportunistic: Plumb uses agent transcript data when available and falls back to diff-only analysis when it is not.
When committing from a bare terminal with no matching session Plumb must fall back to diff-only analysis and still capture decisions derived from code changes rather than reasoning.
The system must prevent duplicate decisions through a multi-stage pipeline using exact matching Jaccard similarity and LLM semantic analysis.
Only prescriptive choices that affect system design behavior architecture or data models must be captured as decisions.
Process observations tooling choices and diagnostic findings must be filtered out from decision capture.
Spec updates must use a search-and-replace approach with edits containing old_text/new_text pairs rather than full section replacement.
Section updates must use exact header matching first then fall back to normalized matching (stripped whitespace case-insensitive) to handle minor variations in header formatting.
Plumb must store all state in a .plumb/ folder at the root of the user's repository and this folder should be committed to version control.
The .plumb/ directory must contain a .gitignore file that ignores record.lock and record.log (runtime files).
The .plumb/ directory must contain a config.json file with spec paths test paths mode and settings.
The .plumb/ directory must contain a decisions/ directory with append-only per-branch decision logs formatted as branch.jsonl files.
The .plumb/ directory must contain a record.lock file used in record mode as an advisory lock held by the extraction worker.
The .plumb/ directory must contain a record.log file in record mode for worker stdout/stderr.
The .plumb/ directory must contain a requirements.json file with cached parsed requirements from the spec.
The ensure_plumb_dir() function must create .plumb/.gitignore listing record.lock and record.log whenever it creates the directory.
Users must track the .gitignore and never the runtime files.
The system must track which requirements have been modified and only send dirty (changed) requirements to the mapper for processing.
Plumb has two modes: review (default) where the pre-commit hook gates commits and record where the post-commit hook extracts decisions outside the commit path.
The effective mode must be resolved in order: PLUMB_MODE environment variable → mode in .plumb/config.json → review.
plumb init must ask which mode to use and plumb mode must show or change the mode.
In review mode the pre-commit hook validates API access before proceeding with analysis and must exit non-zero and block the commit if API authentication fails.

When API authentication fails the system must raise a custom PlumbAuthError exception that alerts the user and provides clear instructions to set their API key via environment variable export or in a .env file.
API key validation must be implemented as a separate validate_api_access function that is called before all LLM operations.
All authentication functionality must have comprehensive test coverage and existing tests must be updated to mock API validation calls.
The hook must analyze the staged diff and the agent transcripts for the repository.
Every registered TraceSource must discover sessions whose recorded cwd resolves to the repository and normalize them into turns.
The hook must write pending decisions to branch-specific decision log files with filesystem-safe path sanitization.
The hook must set the last_extracted_at timestamp when writing pending decisions.
The hook must write a signature of the reviewed staged diff to .plumb/gate.json.
The hook must print a machine-readable JSON summary of pending decisions to stdout and exit non-zero aborting the commit.
Claude Code's skill must read the hook output and begin presenting decisions to the user using AskUserQuestion format one at a time.
The user must respond in the chat and the skill must call the appropriate per-decision command (plumb approve plumb reject or plumb edit).
The system must include explicit safeguards to never approve reject or edit decisions on the user's behalf.
Users must be able to approve multiple pending decisions efficiently using the --all flag with the approve command.
Decision operations must support branch-specific handling through branch parameter support.
For rejected decisions the skill must invoke plumb modify which modifies the staged code runs tests and reports the result conversationally.
Once all decisions are resolved the skill must re-run git commit and the hook must fire again and match the staged diff signature against .plumb/gate.json.
When the hook finds zero pending decisions it must exit zero without any re-analysis and the commit lands.
The commit must only land when there are zero pending decisions.
The system must draft commit messages after decision review and include the list of approved decisions.
The hook must store a reviewed-diff signature whenever it blocks using the first field of git patch-id --stable computed over the filtered staged diff.
An empty filtered diff must use the literal signature empty.
The signature and a creation timestamp must live in .plumb/gate.json.

On a later run the hook must compare the current signature to the stored one and when they match and zero pending decisions remain delete the file and exit zero without reading transcripts or calling the LLM.
When gate state exists but the signature differs the hook must re-run extraction and suppress the diff-only extraction fallback.
.plumb/gate.json must be transient per-machine and gitignored via .plumb/.gitignore.
The post-commit hook must delete .plumb/gate.json after every commit in both modes.
plumb diff and plumb hook --dry-run must neither read nor write .plumb/gate.json.
Diff analysis must exclude .plumb/ the configured spec paths and the configured test paths.
Tests-only commits must produce an empty filtered diff and pass without review.
The tests staged by plumb sync must never read as new work on the second commit attempt.
Decision file_refs must still come from the raw staged hunks and may reference test files.
The pre-commit hook must validate API access before performing any LLM operations and must block commits when authentication fails.
The system must use gitignore-style patterns for ignore functionality with default patterns used when no .plumbignore file exists.
After commit completion the post-commit hook must clear the last_extracted_at timestamp to reset the filter for future extractions and delete .plumb/gate.json to end the review cycle.
Each adapter must handle its agent's native transcript schema and normalize tool usage into ToolCall records.
Tool usage must be rendered for the extractor with file paths commands and truncated results.
The system must implement intelligent deduplication by first running Jaccard similarity filtering then applying LLM deduplication as a second pass when 2 or more candidates remain.
The system must use DSPy's context manager with Haiku LM for deduplication while preserving Sonnet for other operations.
Deduplication must prioritize approved and synced decisions over recent ones in the comparison set.
The system must use an expanded context window of 200 decisions instead of 50 for more comprehensive duplicate detection.
The system must generate complete and runnable tests rather than stub files with TODO comments.
Test generation must use increased context limits to accommodate complete test code.
The test generator must produce fully functional test code that can be executed immediately and only runs if tests don't already exist.
The system must provide read_all_decisions() as the primary API function for accessing decisions across all branches.
The review command must pre-compute decision branches to optimize performance and ensure correct shard targeting for updates.
Users must be able to migrate from the monolithic decision file to the sharded layout using the plumb migrate command to convert existing decisions.jsonl to decisions/main.jsonl.

The system must implement spec updates using a single LLM call per spec file with an output schema containing section_updates and new_sections making a second call only when new_sections is non-empty.
Structural reasoning for section placement must be kept separate from content generation to maintain clarity.
The system must keep edit operations simple without complex operation sets and accept the risk of unintended edits in exchange for performance gains.
The legacy decisions path function must be maintained for migration detection purposes while the primary system operates on branch-specific decision logs.
In Path 2 the pre-commit hook must analyze the staged diff and read the transcripts of every supported agent that recorded this repository as its working directory.
Within-batch similarity deduplication must prevent duplicate decisions in the same batch.
Time awareness must use both last_commit datetime and last_extracted_at timestamp as cutoffs taking the later of the two to determine which conversations to process.
The hook must pass current decisions and recent decisions from the last couple commits to the deduplication pass using a context window of 200 decisions.
The hook must print a human-readable summary of pending decisions and exit non-zero aborting the commit.
The user must run plumb review in their terminal which presents decisions interactively and accepts keypresses.
Rejected decisions must be modifiable via plumb modify which stages the modified code and reports test results.
The user must re-run git commit and the hook must fire again match the reviewed-diff signature find no pending decisions and exit zero without re-analysis.
The commit must land when the user re-runs git commit.
Both paths must use the same hook the same decision log the same per-decision commands and the same sync logic.
The only difference between paths is who drives the review loop: Claude Code's skill or the interactive plumb review CLI.
Agents other than Claude Code must not get the conversational review loop but their sessions must still be read for decisions.
The human must review with plumb review.
The system must use exact deduplication and LLM-based semantic deduplication with groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b configured for both decision_deduplicator and question_synthesizer with 8192 max_tokens.
Source summaries must be structured as per-file mappings to enable granular tracking.
All documentation files including SKILL files and CLAUDE.md must be kept consistent with the same sync workflow requirements.
When the effective mode is record the pre-commit hook must exit 0 immediately without analysis.
plumb diff / plumb hook --dry-run must still preview the staged changes in either mode.

The post-commit hook must record the new HEAD as last_commit as usual then spawn a detached worker plumb record-extract with start_new_session stdin from /dev/null and stdout/stderr appended to .plumb/record.log.
The commit must return immediately and the LLM never runs inside git commit.
The branch must be passed explicitly to plumb record-extract because the user may switch branches before the worker runs.
The worker must take an advisory fcntl lock on .plumb/record.lock so two commits in quick succession extract sequentially and append safely.
While the lock is held plumb status must print Recording in progress.
The worker must run the shared extraction pipeline against the commit's own diff (git show) never the index filtered by managed paths and .plumbignore.
The worker must use git show to get the commit diff not the index.
For a root commit there is no parent so the transcript cutoff must be the Unix epoch (read everything).
Each extracted decision must be written with commit_sha and branch set directly.
When record_threshold is null or the decision's confidence is >= record_threshold it must be written with status=recorded and approved_by=auto.
Otherwise the decision must be written as ordinary pending with approved_by null and never blocks anything.
It must show in plumb status for batch review.

The worker must write nothing (and does not call the LLM) when the commit touches only ignored or Plumb-managed files when it has no patch (e.g. a merge) or when the commit is no longer reachable from any local or remote branch or HEAD.

Before last_commit is overwritten the post-commit hook must compare the new commit with last_commit: if they share a first parent differ and the old commit is no longer on any ref the old commit's decisions (commit_sha == last_commit) must be deleted from the branch shard.
A same-parent sibling whose predecessor still lives on some branch must not be treated as an amend.
The worker must apply the same check when it runs.
Recorded decisions must accumulate unsynced.
plumb status must show the debt (Sync debt: N recorded unsynced).
plumb sync must flush them on demand.
Record mode must never auto-reject or auto-edit.
plumb init must check that the current directory is a git repository and exit with an error if not.
plumb init must create the .plumb/ directory if it does not exist.
plumb init must prompt the user to provide a path to a spec file or directory of spec markdown files and validate that the path exists and contains .md files.
plumb init must use recursive search (rglob) to find markdown files within directories and suggest discovered spec files.
plumb init must prompt the user to provide a path to a test file or test directory and validate that the path exists.
plumb init must scan repository for test directories and files to provide suggestions.
plumb init must prompt the user to choose how Plumb handles decisions with review as default and record as alternative.
plumb init must confirm the inference model with Claude Haiku 4.5 as the default.
On 'n' plumb init must ask for a provider and suggest a litellm model string for that provider.
The answer must be stored as model.
plumb init must validate pytest test collection by checking that pytest is installed.
plumb init must verify test files exist at the specified path.
plumb init must run pytest --collect-only to ensure tests can be collected.
plumb init must handle test_path as either directory or single file using is_dir() vs is_file() checks.
plumb init must skip collection validation for empty test directories to avoid false positives.
On collection failure plumb init must display both stdout and stderr to help user debug and fail fast with SystemExit(1).
plumb init must treat infrastructure issues like TimeoutExpired and FileNotFoundError as warnings not blocking errors.
plumb init must write .plumb/config.json with the provided paths mode and model.
plumb init must create a .plumbignore file in the project root if it does not exist.
plumb init must install the git pre-commit hook by writing a script to .git/hooks/pre-commit that calls plumb hook.
plumb init must set the script as executable.
plumb init must install the Claude Code skill locally by copying plumb/skill/SKILL.md to .claude/skills/plumb/SKILL.md in the project root.
plumb init must create .claude/skills/plumb/ directories if they do not exist.
This must be a project-local installation only and Plumb must never write to the user's global ~/.claude/ directory.
plumb init must append a Plumb status block to CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md at the project root (creating them if they do not exist).
The block must depend on the effective mode.
plumb init must run plumb parse-spec to do an initial parse of the spec into requirements.
plumb init must verify API access for the chosen model with validate_api_access and on failure print the missing credential and exit 1.
Running plumb init again must complete the setup through the clone path.
plumb init must print a confirmation summary to the terminal including confirmation that the skill was installed at .claude/skills/plumb/SKILL.md.
plumb mode with no argument must print the effective mode and its source.
plumb mode with an argument must write mode to config.json reinstall the git hooks and rewrite the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md instruction block to match.
plumb mode must print a confirmation after writing.
If PLUMB_MODE is set to a different value plumb mode must warn that the environment variable overrides the saved mode in the current environment.
plumb mode must exit non-zero for an unknown mode or when Plumb is not initialized.
plumb model with no argument must print the model and its source plus one line per program_models override.
plumb model with an argument must print Testing and check the provider credentials and run a smoke test through validate_api_access.
plumb model must save the model to config.json only on success.
On a failed check plumb model must print the error exit 1 and leave the config unchanged.
plumb model must exit non-zero when Plumb is not initialized.
plumb hook must read .plumb/config.json and if not found exit 0 silently (Plumb not initialized do not block commit).
If the effective mode is record and this is not a dry run plumb hook must exit 0 immediately (extraction happens post-commit).
plumb hook must get the current staged diff via git diff --cached.
plumb hook must get the current branch name.
plumb hook must detect amends by comparing the HEAD commit's parent SHA to last_commit and if equal delete decisions in decisions.jsonl where commit_sha == last_commit before re-running analysis.
plumb hook must detect broken references (rebase) by checking all SHAs in decisions.jsonl against git history and flag unreachable SHAs with ref_status=broken and include a warning in output.
plumb hook must run the Diff Analysis DSPy program on the staged diff.
plumb hook must discover and read agent transcripts for this repository.
If any session is found plumb hook must read turns since the cutoff (the later of last_commit and last_extracted_at).
plumb hook must chunk them per (agent session_id) and run Decision Extraction per chunk.
Each decision must be stamped with provenance (agent session_id parent_session_id source_path turn_range evidence_digest) and deterministic file_refs.
A session that fails to parse must be logged and skipped; the other sessions still load.
If no session is found plumb hook must skip conversation analysis and run extraction on the diff summary alone.
plumb hook must note conversation_available=false and leave agent null in each decision object.
plumb hook must filter out decisions marked as non-spec-relevant during extraction before creating Decision records.
plumb hook must merge and deduplicate decisions across chunks using DuckDB for cross-shard queries to read and deduplicate decisions across all branch JSONL files.
Deduplication must check against all existing decisions (both pending and resolved) instead of only resolved ones.
plumb hook must implement within-batch similarity deduplication to compare new decisions against each other using Jaccard similarity check.
For each decision with no associated question plumb hook must run Question Synthesizer with program-specific model configuration.
plumb hook must write all new decisions with status=pending to decisions.jsonl.
plumb hook must implement decisions sharding using a TDD approach with core refactor DuckDB integration caller updates new commands and comprehensive testing coverage.
plumb hook must run plumb parse-spec to update requirements cache for any modified spec files.
plumb hook must batch spec updates across all decisions instead of running spec update for each individual decision.
plumb hook must use search-and-replace pairs pattern for spec updates where LLM returns list of {old_text new_text} operations instead of rewriting entire sections.
plumb hook must implement a two-tier approach for spec updates: Tier 1 for existing section updates (section-header-keyed replacement) and Tier 2 for structural changes (new sections reordering).
For structural changes plumb hook must use outline-first approach where LLM returns updated header outline first then fills in content for new sections.
plumb hook must create OutlineMerger signature for conditional second call that takes current outline and new headers and returns merged outline with proper positioning.
If pending decisions exist plumb hook must check whether it is running in a TTY (interactive terminal) or as a subprocess (e.g., called by Claude Code).
In TTY plumb hook must print a human-readable summary of pending decisions with instructions to run plumb review.
In non-TTY (subprocess) plumb hook must print a machine-readable JSON object to stdout.
plumb hook must exit non-zero in both cases aborting the commit.
If no pending decisions exist plumb hook must update last_commit and last_commit_branch in config.json and exit 0 allowing the commit to proceed.
The hook must never exit non-zero due to an internal Plumb error and if Plumb itself fails it must print a warning to stderr and exit 0 so the commit is not blocked.
plumb hook --dry-run must run the full hook analysis on staged changes but must not write to decisions.jsonl and must always exit 0.
plumb hook --dry-run must be equivalent to plumb diff and intended for testing and preview.
plumb diff must read staged changes via git diff --cached.
plumb diff must run Diff Analysis on the staged diff.
plumb diff must read and chunk the conversation log (turns since last_commit) if available.
plumb diff must run Decision Extraction per chunk.
plumb diff must print a preview to the terminal with summary of staged code changes estimated number of decisions that would be captured and brief description of each estimated decision.
plumb diff must make no writes to .plumb/.
plumb review must read the decision log across all branch shards and filter for status == pending.
plumb review must accept an optional --branch flag to filter by branch and a --recorded flag.
When multiple session files exist plumb review must use the most recent session file by modification time or match the current session ID for session selection.
If no pending decisions exist plumb review must print No pending decisions. and exit 0.

For each pending decision plumb review must display the framing question the decision made by user or LLM the branch it was made on file and line references whether the commit SHA is reachable (ref_status) and the most related current spec text (if any).
plumb review must prompt the user with [a]pprove [r]eject [e]dit and [s]kip.
After all decisions are resolved plumb review must print a reminder to run plumb sync for all approved/edited decisions.
Approve and edit must set approved_by=user and reviewed_at.
Reject must record the reason and in the pending walk run plumb modify automatically.
plumb review --recorded must walk decisions with status == recorded (the header reads N recorded decision(s); with none No recorded decisions.).
The same approve / ignore / reject / edit prompt must apply to recorded decisions.
Approve must upgrade the decision to approved with approved_by=user.
Edit must amend the text mark it edited and clear synced_at so it re-syncs.
Reject must mark it rejected with the reason and print Code already committed; rejection recorded no automatic modification.
plumb review --recorded must never run plumb modify because the code is already committed and rewriting it is a separate explicit act.
Ignore must be unchanged for recorded decisions.
A rejected recorded decision must keep approved_by=auto (the field records who originally accepted it and survives later status changes).
Decision Classification must default spec_relevant field to True to ensure decisions pass through for user review when LLM classification is uncertain.
plumb approve must approve a single decision by ID and update its status to approved in decisions.jsonl.
plumb approve must then run plumb sync for that decision only.
The status display must include a visual bar chart representation for coverage statistics.
The status display must use Rich's Status spinner that updates in-place for progress indication.
plumb approve must be intended to be called by the Claude Code skill during conversational review.
plumb reject must reject a single decision by ID and update its status to rejected in decisions.jsonl.
plumb reject must record the reason.
plumb reject must not modify code or spec.

plumb reject must be intended to be called by the Claude Code skill during conversational review and after calling this the skill should call plumb modify to resolve the rejected decision in the staged code.
plumb edit must replace the decision text for a given decision ID with the user-provided text and update status to edited.
plumb edit must then run plumb sync for that decision only.
plumb edit must be intended to be called by the Claude Code skill when the user wants to modify what the decision says before approving it.
plumb modify must read the decision object for the given ID from decisions.jsonl and verify status == rejected.
plumb modify must read the staged diff (the code that introduced the decision).

plumb modify must call the Claude API (not a DSPy program) with the staged diff the decision that was made the rejection reason the current spec and an instruction to modify the staged code to satisfy the rejection while keeping behavior consistent with the spec.
plumb modify must apply the proposed modification to the staged files.
plumb modify must run pytest on the test suite to verify that tests still pass after modification.
If tests pass plumb modify must print the resulting diff to the terminal (or return it as JSON in non-TTY mode) stage the modified files and update the decision status to rejected_modified.
If tests fail plumb modify must print the failure output not stage the modification and prompt the user to resolve manually and update decision status to rejected_manual.
In non-TTY mode (Claude Code) plumb modify must return a machine-readable JSON result.
plumb never commits the modification and must only stage it and the user (or Claude Code) must re-run git commit after all decisions are resolved.
plumb sync must add early exit check to avoid expensive operations when no unsynced decisions exist.
plumb sync must read decisions from the decision log with status approved edited or recorded that have not yet been synced (no synced_at timestamp).

For each spec file plumb sync must run WholeFileSpecUpdater processing all decisions affecting the spec file together and returning section_updates for existing sections and new_sections for brand new sections.
If new_sections is non-empty plumb sync must run OutlineMerger to determine proper positioning of new sections within the spec structure.
plumb sync must write the updated spec file to disk (temp file → rename) and fix newline formatting by ensuring proper newlines between section headers and body content.
plumb sync must run Test Generator to generate organized tests for requirements not covered by existing tests.
Tests must be organized by functionality with proper requirement links in the format test__description.
The generator must read only source files referenced by file_refs on synced decisions for context.
plumb sync must write generated tests to test_generated.py (temp file → rename).
plumb sync must run plumb parse-spec to re-cache requirements.
plumb sync must set synced_at on each processed decision.
plumb sync must print a summary of spec sections updated and test files created.
plumb sync must use .plumbignore file with default patterns for documentation build files and IDE configurations to exclude irrelevant files from processing.
plumb parse-spec must read all markdown files in spec_paths from config.json.
For each file or paragraph block plumb parse-spec must run Requirement Parser to produce explicit testable requirement statements.
plumb parse-spec must assign each requirement a stable ID based on a hash of its content.

plumb parse-spec must write results to .plumb/requirements.json and requirements with matching hashes must not be re-processed preserving existing metadata including created_at and last_seen_commit timestamps.
plumb parse-spec must use regex patterns PLUMB_MARKER_RE and FUNC_NAME_RE to extract requirement IDs from test files for coverage mapping.
plumb parse-spec must process all requirements and AST summaries of every non-test .py file through the CodeCoverageMapper using chunked mapping approach to avoid context overflow.
plumb parse-spec must use fan-out chunking to group source files under token budget (default 60000 tokens) and broadcast requirements to each chunk.
plumb parse-spec must implement granular per-file hashing with structured v2 cache format that tracks individual requirement results for efficient cache invalidation.
plumb parse-spec must preserve existing incremental caching logic by applying chunking inside the LLM call after dirty requirements are determined.
plumb parse-spec must extract source file paths from evidence strings using pattern matching against known files to determine requirement-to-file mappings.
plumb parse-spec must use greedy packing to group source/test summaries into chunks and ThreadPoolExecutor for concurrent chunk processing.
plumb parse-spec must merge results from multiple chunks using custom logic that ORs 'implemented' flags and concatenates evidence strings per requirement_id.
plumb coverage must run pytest --cov and parse output for line coverage percentage.

plumb coverage must report spec-to-test coverage by checking whether each requirement in the cache has a test that references or maps to it using string-matching to look for requirement IDs (like 'req-79c36afc') literally in test files.
plumb coverage must scan for link markers in test files to determine coverage.
plumb coverage must report spec-to-code coverage by checking whether each requirement has a corresponding implementation using string-matching to look for requirement IDs literally in source files.
plumb coverage must print a formatted table using rich.
plumb coverage must use LLM calls to refresh the requirements cache for accurate coverage analysis.
plumb coverage must measure and report coverage improvement achieved by marker injection.
plumb log must show the decision log grouped by commit then by agent and be read-only unless --verify finds a definitive answer.
plumb log must read all decisions across every branch shard excluding ignored sorted by created_at then id so output is reproducible.
plumb log --since must keep only decisions whose commit_sha is in the reference range and uncommitted decisions (commit_sha null) are always shown.

plumb log must group by commit_sha (uncommitted first then commits newest first) then by agent (unknown when null e.g. diff-only decisions) and print each decision's id status made_by confidence session id and turn range.
plumb log --verify must re-read each decision's transcript at source_path with the same adapter and no cutoff and apply the per-turn transforms the hook applied (prepare_for_digest).

plumb log --verify must recompute the sha256 digest over turn_range and report one of: ok stale (digest mismatch or the range is gone) missing (transcript file no longer exists) or unverifiable (no provenance unknown agent or parse failure).
Only ok and stale must be written back to ref_status.
missing and unverifiable must leave it alone and a broken ref must never be overwritten.
plumb search must search the decision log across every branch and print a flat list as the counterpart to plumb log's grouped view and be read-only.
plumb search must use enumeration as one DuckDB query over .plumb/decisions/*.jsonl with explicit column types and latest-line-wins dedup.
Every filter must be a SQL WHERE clause: --status and --agent are repeatable; --file must match file_refs[*].file; --since must accept an ISO date or a git ref (resolved to that commit's datetime).
Sorting and --limit (default 50; 0 = all) must be applied in SQL.
With no --status ignored and every rejected* status must be hidden.
Relevance must be BM25 over question + decision + user_note computed in process.
Default sort must be relevance when a query is given and date (newest first) otherwise.
--sort relevance without a query must fall back to date.
--sort confidence must order by confidence descending nulls last.
plumb search output rows must show id status agent made_by confidence date short commit session/turn range when present the decision text and matched file refs.
--json must emit the full Decision records.
plumb record-extract must be the record-mode worker and be launched by the post-commit hook and not intended to be called by users but must work if called manually (e.g. to backfill a commit).
plumb record-extract must take the .plumb/record.lock advisory lock then run the extraction described under Path 3 for the given SHA.
plumb record-extract must write to the --branch shard (default: the checked-out branch).
plumb record-extract must print Recorded N decision(s) M pending for.
plumb record-extract --wait must be accepted for compatibility; the command must always run inline once it holds the lock.
plumb record-extract must exit non-zero outside a git repository or when Plumb is not initialized.
plumb status must print a human-readable summary including Mode (from env|config|default).
In record mode plumb status must print Recording in progress… while a worker holds .plumb/record.lock.
plumb status must print tracked spec files and total requirements.
plumb status must print the number of tests.
plumb status must print pending decisions with branch breakdown if spanning multiple branches.
plumb status must print Sync debt: N recorded unsynced (run 'plumb sync') when recorded decisions have no synced_at (omitted when there are none).
plumb status must print decisions with broken git references.
plumb status must print last sync commit.
plumb status must print coverage summary (all three dimensions).
The Claude Code skill must be at plumb/skill/SKILL.md in the package and during plumb init copied to .claude/SKILL.md in the project root as a project-local installation only.
The skill file must not be installed globally.
Claude Code must automatically read files in .claude/ at the start of each session.
The skill file must provide structured guidance for AI-assisted development workflow.
The skill file must teach Claude Code the Plumb workflow so it can guide the user naturally through the development process.
The skill file must provide the machine-readable protocol for parsing hook output and calling per-decision commands during conversational review.
Transcript discovery and parsing must not be the skill's job; they must live in the plumb/traces/ adapters.
The .claude/ directory and SKILL.md must be committed to version control so all contributors to the project get the skill automatically.
Before starting work the user must run plumb status to understand the current state of spec/test/code alignment.
The user must note any pending decisions and any broken git references.
The user must report a brief summary before proceeding.
Before committing the user must run plumb diff to preview what Plumb will capture from staged changes.
The user must report the estimated decisions so they are not surprised during review.
When git commit is intercepted the user must parse the JSON from stdout with pending_decisions and decisions array.
The user must present each decision conversationally one at a time using structured format.
All decisions must be explicitly reviewed and approved by the user and no decisions shall be automatically approved without explicit user instruction.
Based on the user's response the user must call the appropriate command: plumb approve plumb reject or plumb edit.
For rejections the system must automatically call plumb modify and parse its JSON output.
If tests_passed is true the user must confirm the change looks correct before proceeding.
If tests_passed is false the user must resolve the issue manually and the decision status will be rejected_manual.
Rejected decisions must be marked with ignored status rather than being deleted from the system.
Once all decisions are resolved the user must run plumb sync to update the spec with approved decisions before re-running git commit.
The hook must fire again and if there are no pending decisions it must exit 0 and the commit must land.
If new decisions are found (rare) the review process must repeat.
The sync operation must identify and use the correct decision branch when marking decisions as synced.
All CLI operations must require explicit user commands and the system shall not perform automatic synchronization or background operations without direct user instruction.
After committing the user must run plumb coverage and briefly report the three coverage dimensions to the user: code coverage spec-to-test coverage and spec-to-code coverage.
The user must flag any gaps that should be addressed before the next commit.
When the user asks what to work on next the user must run plumb coverage to identify requirements with no corresponding tests (run plumb parse-spec first if the spec has changed).
The user must identify requirements with no corresponding implementation and code with no test coverage.
The user must present these gaps clearly so the user can prioritize.
The user must never edit .plumb/decisions.jsonl directly.
The user must never edit .plumb/config.json directly and must use plumb init or plumb status instead.
The user must never install the Plumb skill globally (~/.claude/) as it is project-local only.
The spec markdown files must be the source of truth for intended behavior and Plumb must keep them updated as decisions are approved.
The user must not edit spec files to resolve decisions but let Plumb do it via plumb sync.
The user must not attempt to commit if there are decisions with status=rejected_manual as the user must resolve these manually first.
When handling decision conflicts the user must use opposite ordering rules: for duplicate decisions keep the earlier one (lower index); for countermanded decisions keep the later one (higher index).
The user must use section-header-keyed full replacement instead of search-and-replace for markdown spec editing.
Plumb must be installable via both pip and uv using the package name plumb-dev.
The CLI command must be plumb.
The package must include a comprehensive project description sourced from the README.md file to provide clear information on PyPI about the library's purpose and functionality.
README.md must be included in the project configuration in pyproject.toml.
Tests must support two formats for linking to requirements: comment-based markers using # plumb:req-XXXXXXXX format and function name-based linking using test_req_XXXXXXXX_ format.
Both formats must be supported for backwards compatibility.
The system must filter for spec-relevant content during decision extraction in both conversation analysis and diff analysis methods to ensure only pertinent decisions are processed.
The system must implement semantic similarity checking to handle duplicate or similar decisions effectively.
Classification tasks must not generate reasoning traces to maintain optimal performance.
LLM-based deduplication must utilize Claude Haiku 4.5 as the designated model.
The deduplicate_decisions() function must accept a use_llm parameter that defaults to False to ensure backward compatibility while enabling optional LLM-based deduplication.
The deduplication function must include fallback handling for truncated or failed LLM responses by returning all candidates when the LLM returns None or produces truncated output.
The LLM deduplicator must return the indices of candidates to remove (duplicate or countermanded) so an empty or missing answer degrades to keeping everything.
An LLM-proposed removal must additionally be corroborated by lexical overlap (token Jaccard ≥ 0.3) with some existing decision or another candidate.
An uncorroborated removal must be vetoed and the candidate kept because silently dropping a genuinely new decision is worse than keeping a near-duplicate.
Plumb must integrate with git hooks to automatically trigger workflows based on repository events.
This must enable seamless integration into the development process without requiring manual intervention.
DSPy programs must support program-specific model configuration through a model configuration array in config.json.
Pattern parsing logic must be modularized into separate functions for reusability across programs including an extract_outline function that extracts markdown headers from content.
The programs module must include token estimation chunking and concurrent mapper functionality to handle large datasets by breaking them into token-budget-sized chunks.
The system must use chunked mapping with ThreadPoolExecutor for concurrent processing and support different merge strategies for result combination.
The .plumb/ folder should be committed to version control.
dspy must be a dependency for LLM workflow programs and framework for implementing LLM-based components.
litellm must be a dependency for provider-neutral inference calls.
pytest must be a dependency for test running.
pytest-cov must be a dependency for coverage reporting.
gitpython must be a dependency for git history and diff access.
click must be a dependency for CLI framework.
rich must be a dependency for terminal output formatting.
jsonlines must be a dependency for reading/writing .jsonl decision logs.
The plumb/cli.py file must be the Click CLI entrypoint.
The plumb/config.py file must handle config loading/saving (.plumb/config.json).
The plumb/git_hook.py file must handle the git pre-commit hook installer and runner.
The plumb/conversation.py file must handle agent-agnostic turn rendering per-session chunking and evidence digests.
The plumb/log_view.py file must handle grouping and evidence verification behind plumb log.
The plumb/traces/ directory must contain TraceSource adapters to find and normalize agent transcripts.
The plumb/traces/__init__.py file must contain SessionRef ToolCall Turn TraceSource protocol and all_sources().
The plumb/traces/claude.py file must be the Claude Code adapter.
The plumb/traces/codex.py file must be the Codex rollout adapter.
The plumb/traces/pi.py file must be the Pi adapter (active-ancestry walk).
The plumb/traces/copilot.py file must be the Copilot CLI adapter (unverified against live sessions).
The plumb/traces/taxonomy.py file must contain the nine-category tool taxonomy and path/summary extraction.
The plumb/traces/repo.py file must handle cwd-to-repo matching via git-common-dir and cutoff helpers.
The plumb/traces/hunks.py file must handle staged hunk parsing and deterministic file_refs.
The plumb/traces/jsonl.py file must contain tolerant JSONL helpers.
The plumb/decision_log.py file must handle read/write .plumb/decisions.jsonl.
The plumb/coverage_reporter.py file must handle code spec and test coverage analysis.
The plumb/sync.py file must handle spec and test sync logic.
The plumb/programs/ directory must contain DSPy programs using Predict pattern.
The plumb/programs/__init__.py file must be in the programs directory.
The plumb/programs/diff_analyzer.py file must cluster and summarize git diffs (excludes Plumb-managed files).
The plumb/programs/decision_extractor.py file must extract decisions/questions from conversation chunks.
The plumb/programs/requirement_parser.py file must convert spec markdown into explicit requirements.
The plumb/programs/spec_updater.py file must rewrite spec to reflect approved decisions.
The plumb/programs/test_generator.py file must generate pytest tests for uncovered requirements.
The plumb/programs/code_modifier.py file must modify staged code to satisfy rejected decisions.
The plumb/skill/ directory must contain the SKILL.md Claude Code skill file.
The plumb/skill/SKILL.md file must be installed locally on plumb init.
SessionRef must contain agent session_id path cwd branch and parent_session_id.
Turn must contain agent session_id ordinal role content timestamp and tool_calls.
ordinal must be the turn's position within its session and must be stable across runs.
ToolCall must contain name category file_path file_paths input_summary result_summary and tool_use_id.
file_paths must list every path a multi-file edit touches (e.g. Codex apply_patch).
file_path must be the first entry of file_paths.
Discovery must not encode the repository path into a directory name.
For every adapter the discovery must glob the agent's candidate files whose mtime is after the cutoff.
The discovery must read the file head for the working directory the agent recorded (cwd).

The discovery must keep the session if that cwd resolves to the same repository as repo_root compared on git rev-parse --git-common-dir (not --show-toplevel) so a linked worktree attributes to its main repository.
If no session matches Plumb must skip conversation analysis note conversation_available=false in each decision print a warning and continue with diff-only analysis.
Plumb must read only turns recorded after the cutoff: the later of the last_commit commit time and last_extracted_at in config.json.
A source or session that fails to discover or parse must be logged and skipped; the remaining sessions still load.
There must be no claude_log_path config key and no legacy log path.
Every tool call must be classified into one of nine categories: Read Edit Write Bash Grep Glob Task Tool Other.
The mapping from each agent's raw tool names must live in plumb/traces/taxonomy.py.
Unknown names must fall through to Other and be still emitted.
file_path/file_paths must be extracted for Read/Edit/Write from the agent-specific argument (file_path path or the patch headers of apply_patch).
Chunk text must keep the [role]: content form.
Tool calls must render with substance rather than as [tool: Name].
An Edit must render with its file path a Bash call with its command and a truncated result and so on.
Chunking must be performed in conversation.py before any DSPy program is called.
No LLM must be involved in chunking (chunks are created deterministically).
Per-session segmentation must group turns by (agent session_id) in first-seen order before chunking.
Sessions must never be interleaved.
Subagent sessions must be chunked as their own sessions with parent_session_id set (from the SessionRef).
The primary unit must be: within a session a chunk is one user message plus all following assistant turns up to but not including the next user message.
If a chunk exceeds DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS (6,000 estimated tokens) it must split at turn boundaries into groups that fit.
A single turn whose rendering alone exceeds the budget must be truncated to DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS * 4 characters and the chunk must be marked truncated.
This truncation is the one pre-digest transform besides noise reduction so plumb log --verify can reproduce it.
Each chunk's text must begin with [agent= session= parent= turns -] (the parent= field is present only for subagent sessions) so the extractor can attribute made_by and so provenance round-trips.
The final turn of the previous chunk of the same session must be prepended as one turn of overlap.
turn_start/turn_end must exclude the overlap so provenance points at new content only.

Before chunking replace tool result turns longer than 500 tokens whose content appears to be a raw file read (heuristic: content begins with a file path or code fence) must be replaced with [file read: ].
Claude Code must write one content block per JSONL entry so a single assistant message (its text plus its tool calls) spans several consecutive assistant entries that share a message.id.

The Claude adapter must merge those consecutive entries into one assistant turn: text blocks are joined tool calls are appended in order the first entry's timestamp is kept and the ordinal is not advanced.
A user turn between two entries must end the merge and entries without a message.id must never be merged.
chunk_index must be the chunk's position in this run only and must not be stored on decisions.
DecisionExtractor must be called once per chunk with the diff_summary passed identically to every call.

Results must be merged after all chunks: near-duplicate decisions (same question + substantively same decision) must be collapsed into one preserving the earliest occurrence (by session order then turn ordinal).
Deterministic enrichment must have no model calls and must cover only turn_start..turn_end never the overlap turn so they are reproducible from (source_path turn_range) alone.
file_refs must be the file_paths of every Edit/Write tool call in the range intersected with the files that have staged hunks.
Relative paths must be resolved against the session's cwd.
Paths outside the repository must be dropped.
One FileRef must be emitted per staged hunk with lines = [start end] from the hunk header.
evidence_digest must be sha256 over the rendered turns in the range after prepare_for_digest (noise reduction ordinal order single-turn truncation).
The header and overlap must not be included in the evidence_digest.
agent session_id parent_session_id source_path and turn_range = [turn_start turn_end] must be copied from the chunk and its SessionRef.
agent must be null for diff-only decisions.

In review mode the pre-commit hook must fire on amends and to prevent duplicates must compare HEAD's parent SHA to last_commit and if equal must delete decisions where commit_sha == last_commit before re-running analysis.

In record mode the check must run post-commit against a commit that actually exists: if the new commit and last_commit share a first parent differ and the old commit is on no local or remote ref the old commit's decisions must be deleted before the worker re-extracts.
On every hook run the system must check all stored SHAs against git history and unreachable SHAs must be flagged ref_status=broken.
Plumb must not attempt to re-map decisions to new SHAs and the user must review and re-resolve broken-reference decisions manually.
The decision log must be append-only and existing lines must never be modified in place.
Status updates must be written as new lines with the same id and the latest line for a given id must be canonical.
Datetime fields (created_at synced_at reviewed_at) must be stored and round-tripped as ISO-8601 strings.

The decision_log.py module must handle serialization and deserialization of datetime and date types to ensure proper conversion between Python datetime objects and ISO-8601 string representations for JSON compatibility.

Provenance fields must be agent ("claude" | "codex" | "pi" | "copilot" null for diff-only decisions) session_id parent_session_id (set for subagent sessions) source_path (transcript file) and turn_range ([start end] ordinals within that session) and evidence_digest (sha256 of the rendered turns in turn_range).
chunk_index must be deprecated: it must be kept in the schema for old rows but the hook must no longer populate it.
Status values must be pending | approved | edited | recorded | rejected | rejected_modified | rejected_manual.
recorded must be written by record mode with the commit SHA set directly and syncs like approved and counts as an existing decision for dedup.
approved_by values must be "user" | "auto" (user when a human approved or edited the decision; auto when record mode recorded it).
approved_by must be set once and preserved across later status changes so provenance survives when a recorded decision is upgraded.
approved_by must be null while pending.
ref_status values must be ok | broken | stale.
stale must mean the evidence digest no longer matches the transcript at source_path / turn_range and must be set and cleared by plumb log --verify.
made_by values must be "user" | "agent" (user if human stated or confirmed the decision agent otherwise).
In review mode commit_sha must be null until the commit lands.
Record mode must set commit_sha directly because the commit already exists.

The post-commit hook must stamp commit_sha: every decision on the current branch with a null commit_sha and a created_at after the previous last_commit's commit time must be updated with the new HEAD SHA (ignored decisions are skipped).
plumb log must group on commit_sha field.
DiffAnalyzer Input must be raw unified diff string.

DiffAnalyzer Output must be list of change summaries each with files_changed (list of filenames) summary (one-sentence description) and change_type ("feature" | "bugfix" | "refactor" | "test" | "spec" | "config" | "other").
DiffAnalyzer must group related changes into logical units and not invent meaning.
DecisionExtractor Input must be chunk (single conversation chunk) and diff_summary (output of DiffAnalyzer identical across all chunk calls).
DecisionExtractor Output must be list of decision objects with question decision made_by ("user" | "agent") confidence and spec_relevant.

DecisionExtractor must extract explicit and implicit decisions from conversation chunks and code diffs and parse and preserve full tool call data from transcripts with category tool_name file_path and input fields.
DecisionExtractor must use agentsview's 9-category tool taxonomy to structure tool information and maintain truncated results for Bash and Edit operations.
DecisionExtractor must not extract trivial decisions (variable naming import ordering).
QuestionSynthesizer Input must be a decision object with no associated question.
QuestionSynthesizer Output must be a plain-English question framing the decision for a developer.
RequirementParser Input must be markdown string.
RequirementParser Output must be list of requirement objects with text and ambiguous fields.
RequirementParser must enforce: atomic statements active voice no duplicates and vague statements must be flagged ambiguous: true and excluded unless user approves.
SpecUpdater Input must be spec_section (markdown) and decision (approved decision object).
SpecUpdater Output must be updated markdown for that section.
SpecUpdater Rules must be: result of decision captured as natural requirement; no reference to the decision itself; existing formatting preserved.
TestGenerator Input must be requirements (uncovered) existing_tests (file contents) and code_context (relevant source).
TestGenerator Output must be runnable pytest test code as a Python string.

TestGenerator Rules must be: one function per requirement descriptive names (test__description) tests contain real assertions against actual code under test no pytest.skip() or # TODO: implement and no overwriting existing tests.

CodeModifier must be used by plumb modify and must be litellm (not DSPy) as this is the one place in Plumb where an open-ended agent call is used rather than a DSPy program because code modification is inherently open-ended.
CodeModifier Input must be staged diff rejected decision rejection reason and current spec.
CodeModifier Output must be modified file contents that satisfy the rejection while remaining consistent with the spec.

CodeModifier must be called through litellm.completion with a structured prompt and the model must come from program_models["code_modifier"] when configured and otherwise from the config model with max_tokens set to 16000.
CodeModifier must parse the message content of the first choice and Plumb must apply the output run pytest and stage the result only if tests pass.
All CLI commands must fail gracefully with a clear error message if config.json is missing or malformed.
All DSPy programs must retry on LLM failure (max 2 retries) then raise PlumbInferenceError with a human-readable message.
The git hook must never exit non-zero due to an internal Plumb error and failures must print a warning to stderr and exit 0.
File writes (spec updates test generation) must use temp file → rename to avoid partial writes.
If conversation log is unavailable Plumb must continue with diff-only analysis and this is not an error.
If plumb modify test run fails Plumb must not stage the modification and must update decision status to rejected_manual.
The plumb status command must operate in cache-only mode to avoid making LLM calls.
The plumb coverage command must display progress using an in-place updating spinner then print the final results table.
Session file reading must be optimized by pre-filtering based on file modification times to skip files that cannot contain relevant conversations.
Plumb testing must use pytest with 80% coverage minimum for v0.1.0.

cli.py tests must verify all commands run without error given valid inputs and per-decision commands update decisions.jsonl correctly and coverage command provides progress feedback with progress bar and status text and spec and test suggestion functions cover various directory scenarios.
decision_log.py tests must verify read/write/filter/dedup on .jsonl and latest-line-wins logic for status updates.
git_hook.py tests must verify hook produces correct pending decisions given mock diffs and conversation logs and amend detection and TTY vs non-TTY output formats.

conversation.py tests must verify correct per-session chunk boundaries header overlap noise reduction metadata and oversized turns truncated and flagged and evidence digest reproducible via prepare_for_digest.

traces/ tests must verify each adapter parses fixture transcripts into Turn/ToolCall records and cwd discovery matches on git-common-dir and taxonomy and path extraction and staged hunk parsing and file_refs.
log_view.py tests must verify grouping order and verify_evidence returns ok/stale/missing/unverifiable correctly.

programs/ tests must verify each DSPy program produces correctly structured output given fixture inputs (schema validity not LLM quality) and comprehensive test suite for chunking functionality covering token estimation item chunking and chunked mapper execution scenarios.
coverage_reporter.py tests must verify correct calculations given mock pytest output.

sync.py tests must verify spec and test files updated correctly given approved decisions and no partial writes and newline formatting tests covering both apply_section_updates() and insert_new_sections() functions.

Out of scope for v0.1.0 are: Web UI or dashboard; Support for non-Python projects or non-pytest test frameworks; Multi-user or team sync features; Undoing decisions that are already committed (users should use their coding agent and commit; the resulting spec conflict will be surfaced during the next review); Integration with issue trackers (GitHub Issues Linear etc.); Automatic re-mapping of decisions to new SHAs after a rebase.
The conversation log reader must work seamlessly across different repositories without requiring additional user setup or configuration overhead.
